reviews.reason: The supplied Geʿez agrees with the chapter XXIX opening in the scan. The English preserves its movement and directional wording without silently substituting the Greek construction. Notes a, b and c have appropriate anchors and disclose the directional ambiguity.

Two printed critical daggers have been transcribed as Geʿez ተ: the scan reads †ኵነኔ and †ፈድፋደ, not ተኵነኔ and ተፈድፋደ. Retaining judgment faithfully distinguishes the printed reading from the fragrant conjecture, provided its corruption marking remains explicit. The untranslated bracketed word needs disclosure. Only the final comparison noun is parenthesized and supplied, not the entire resemblance clause. The cross-page continuation ይትማሰሉ followed by the parenthesized noun ends before XXX, proving the chapter boundary.
reviews.suggested_text: And there I saw trees of judgment[a], giving off[b] the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh; and their trees resembled nut-bearing trees[c].
reviews.footnote_changes:
a: The printed Geʿez has †ኵነኔ, judgment, marked as corrupt; the printed Greek likewise has κρίσεως. Charles proposes fragrant in printed page 69 notes 14 and 27. That is an editorial conjecture, not the reading printed in either main text. Judgment remains semantically difficult.
b: Attach this marker immediately to giving off. The Geʿez †ፈድፋደ is marked corrupt; note 28 proposes a repair corresponding to the printed Greek πνέοντα. Giving off follows that interpretation rather than an unproblematic Geʿez reading. The following bracketed word [ቈስቍስ፡] is not translated here: note 29 calls it unintelligible and treats it as an intrusion if the Greek is correct, while also considering whether it preserves a corrupted tree name.
c: The final parenthesized Geʿez comparison noun is supplied by Charles with assistance from the Greek; the preceding words their trees resembled are not themselves a parenthesized supply. Printed page 69 notes 18 and 29 explain the omission and possible displaced, corrupted counterpart in Ethiopic; printed page 70 note 2 refers back to note 29. Nut-bearing trees renders Greek καρύαις without fixing a species. Charles discusses almond-tree or almond-nut, but that identification is not established by the printed comparison alone.
reviews.suggested_source_text: Replace ተኵነኔ፡ with †ኵነኔ፡ and ተፈድፋደ፡ with †ፈድፋደ፡. Retain the square brackets around ቈስቍስ፡ and parentheses around the final supplied noun. Restore the printed terminal double colon inside those parentheses: (ከርካዕ።).
